label: IMI-RHAPSODY
definition: An Innovative Medicines Initiative consortium that generated molecular data across large European diabetes cohorts to identify markers of progression from pre-diabetes to type 2 diabetes and of glycaemic deterioration measured as time to insulin initiation.

label: IMMUcan
definition: An Innovative Medicines Initiative consortium that builds prospective cohorts of cancer patients, including head and neck, lung and breast cancer cohorts, with integrated tumour immune profiling and longitudinal clinical data to understand how the immune system interacts with tumours and therapy.

label: IMMUcan SCCHN1 cohort
definition: A cohort of patients with locally recurrent or metastatic squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck receiving first-line immune checkpoint inhibitors, with or without chemotherapy, profiled by the IMMUcan consortium with multiplex imaging, mass cytometry and sequencing alongside longitudinal clinical data.

label: ImmunAID
definition: A multicentre cohort of patients with systemic autoinflammatory diseases recruited across several European cohorts by the ImmunAID Horizon 2020 project, with integrated immunological and molecular data to identify diagnostic biomarkers and disease pathways.

label: Initiative for Molecular Profiling and Advanced Cancer Therapy 2
definition: A cohort of patients with metastatic cancer who underwent tumour genomic profiling in IMPACT2, a randomised study at MD Anderson Cancer Center evaluating genomic profiling and matched targeted therapy.

label: International Cancer Genome Consortium
definition: An international consortium of cancer genome projects, each characterising the somatic and germline genomes of a tumour type in a defined population, that coordinates the projects' data and analyses, including the Pan-Cancer Analysis of Whole Genomes.

label: International Genetics of Parkinson Disease Progression Consortium
definition: A consortium of longitudinal Parkinson's disease cohorts, including EPIPARK and the Harvard Biomarkers Study, that pools prospectively followed patients for genome-wide survival studies of progression to dementia and other outcomes.

label: International HapMap Project
definition: A collection of DNA samples and cell lines from populations of African, Asian and European ancestry assembled by the International HapMap Project to map common patterns of human genetic variation, which serves as a reference panel and control set for genetic studies.

label: InterPregGen
definition: A consortium funded under the European Seventh Framework Programme that grew out of the WTCCC3 pre-eclampsia GWAS and combines maternal and fetal pre-eclampsia case-control collections from Europe and Central Asia for genome-wide meta-analyses.

label: Korean Genome Project
definition: A cohort of Koreans whose whole genomes are sequenced by the Korean Genome Project, 4,157 of whom form the Korea4K resource with 107 health check-up parameters for genome-phenome association studies.

label: LifeLines-DEEP
definition: A sub-cohort of approximately 1,500 LifeLines participants from the northern Netherlands who provided additional biological materials, including gut microbiome samples, for multi-omic investigation of the factors that contribute to health and disease.

label: Lifelines-NEXT
definition: A birth cohort of approximately 1,500 newborns and their mothers from the three northern provinces of the Netherlands, nested in LifeLines and followed from pregnancy through the first year of life and beyond with microbiome and virome sampling.

label: Liverpool Preterm Birth Biomarker Study
definition: A cohort of 567 women with singleton pregnancies recruited at the Liverpool Women's Hospital at 16 and 20 weeks of gestation, with genome-wide genotypes and blood transcriptomes, to identify early pregnancy biomarkers of spontaneous preterm birth and preterm premature rupture of membranes.

label: Low coverage Kuusamo whole genome sequencing study
definition: A subset of the FINRISK 2012 sample collection consisting of participants recruited in Kuusamo, Finland, whose genomes were sequenced at 1x coverage.

label: Lung Cancer Diagnostic Study
definition: A prospective cohort of 365 individuals at risk of lung cancer, of whom 129 were diagnosed with lung cancer, recruited at Bispebjerg Hospital in Copenhagen, Denmark, for cell-free DNA fragmentation analysis to detect and characterise lung cancer.

label: lungNENomics
definition: A cohort of patients with lung neuroendocrine neoplasms, including typical and atypical carcinoids, assembled by the IARC-led lungNENomics project for whole-genome, transcriptome and methylation profiling to characterise these tumours molecularly.

label: Maastricht IBS studies
definition: A collection of irritable bowel syndrome cases and controls from studies at Maastricht University Medical Centre, the Netherlands, whose gut microbiomes were characterised by metagenomic sequencing.

label: Malaria Genomic Epidemiology Network
definition: An international network of investigators that assembles samples and data from malaria-endemic countries in Africa, Asia and Oceania to study the genomic epidemiology of malaria, including a low-coverage whole-genome sequence reference set of African ethnic groups.

label: Malaysian Breast Cancer cohort
definition: A hospital-based cohort of breast cancer patients in Malaysia whose tumours, including triple-negative cancers, have been characterised by exome and RNA sequencing to develop classifiers such as a gene signature for homologous recombination deficiency.

label: Malmö Diet and Cancer Study
definition: A population-based prospective cohort of about 30,000 residents of Malmö, Sweden, born 1923–1950 and recruited during 1991–1996 with dietary, lifestyle, clinical and genetic data to investigate diet, cancer and cardiovascular disease.

label: Mechanisms of the Development of Allergy
definition: A European Union Seventh Framework Programme project that combines European birth cohorts, including INMA, EDEN, BAMSE and PIAMA, to investigate the mechanisms of the development of allergy through harmonised phenotypes and epigenetic and other omic measurements.

label: Medical Genome Reference Bank
definition: A whole-genome sequence resource of 4,000 healthy individuals aged 60 to 95 with no history of cancer, cardiovascular disease or dementia, recruited from two Australian community-based cohorts to serve as a reference population depleted of pathogenic alleles.

label: MESOMICS
definition: A collection of malignant pleural mesothelioma samples from the French MESOMICS project, characterised by whole-genome sequencing, RNA sequencing and methylation arrays.

label: Milan cohort
definition: A cohort of breast cancer patients from Milan, Italy, whose ductal carcinoma in situ and invasive breast cancers were compared by subtype at the levels of gene expression, copy number and methylation.

label: Milieu Intérieur
definition: A population-based cohort of 1,000 healthy individuals of western European ancestry recruited in France by the Institut Pasteur's Milieu Intérieur project to dissect the interplay between genetics, environment and the immune system.

label: MITO16A/MaNGO-OV2 trial
definition: A cohort of 398 patients with ovarian cancer enrolled at 47 centres in the single-arm phase IV MITO16A/MaNGO-OV2 trial of first-line carboplatin, paclitaxel and bevacizumab, studied for clinical and biological prognostic factors.

label: Molecular Phenotyping to Accelerate Genomic Epidemiology
definition: An integrated European Union project that developed methods and tools for discovering biomarkers of diabetes, drawing on sub-studies of the Oxford Biobank (MolOBB) and TwinsUK (MolTWIN).

label: Molecular Taxonomy of Breast Cancer International Consortium
definition: A collection of about 2,000 primary breast tumours with long-term clinical follow-up from tumour banks in the United Kingdom and Canada, profiled for copy number and gene expression to derive a molecular stratification of breast cancer.

label: MRCE family panel
definition: A family panel of 550 individuals from asthma families whose genome-wide SNP genotypes and whole-genome expression profiles extended the MRCA family panel's map of expression quantitative trait loci.

label: MultiMuTHER
definition: A longitudinal sub-study of 335 TwinsUK women from the Multiple Tissue Human Expression Resource, seen at three or more clinical visits over up to nine years with repeated whole-blood gene expression and serum metabolite profiling to characterise molecular ageing.

label: Multiple Tissue Human Expression Resource
definition: A sub-cohort of adult female TwinsUK participants from whom adipose, skin, lymphoblastoid cell line and blood samples were collected to map genetic and epigenetic regulation of gene expression across tissues.

label: Nala GSI GSAv3 PGx Study
definition: A pre-clinical validation study of a pharmacogenomic genotyping workflow on the Illumina Global Screening Array, performed on 73 reference cell lines from the Genome in a Bottle, GeT-RM and 1000 Genomes collections rather than on recruited participants.

label: NCI China cohort
definition: A cohort of Chinese patients with and without bladder or lung cancer, exposed to diesel exhaust or polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, who provided buccal and urothelial cells for duplex sequencing of somatic mutations in a collaboration between the United States National Cancer Institute and IARC.

label: NCI Taiwan cohort
definition: A cohort of patients in Taiwan with and without oral cancer, dysplasia and risk factors for oral cancer who provided buccal cells for duplex sequencing of somatic mutations in a collaboration between the United States National Cancer Institute and IARC.

label: NeoALTTO
definition: A cohort of women with HER2-positive breast cancer enrolled in the NeoALTTO phase III trial of neoadjuvant paclitaxel with trastuzumab and/or lapatinib, whose tumour B and T cell receptor repertoires were profiled to identify prognostic immune features.

label: NIHR BioResource
definition: A National Institute for Health and Care Research resource of volunteers in England recallable by genotype and phenotype, including blood donors and patients with common and rare diseases, whose genotype data support health research.

label: Pan-Cancer Analysis of Whole Genomes
definition: An international collaboration of the International Cancer Genome Consortium and The Cancer Genome Atlas that analysed more than 2,800 cancer whole genomes from the consortia's projects to identify common patterns of somatic and germline variation in coding and non-coding regions.

label: PANDA trial
definition: A cohort of 21 patients with previously untreated resectable gastric or gastro-oesophageal junction adenocarcinoma treated in the phase 2 PANDA trial with neoadjuvant atezolizumab and chemotherapy, sampled at multiple time points to study the tumour microenvironment.

label: PELICAN
definition: An integrated clinical-molecular rapid autopsy study of men who died of lethal prostate cancer at Johns Hopkins, United States, whose primary and metastatic tumours and normal tissues were collected for sequencing.

label: PETAL trial
definition: A cohort of patients with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma treated in the German PETAL trial of PET-guided therapy, whose tumours were exome and shallow whole-genome sequenced to reproduce biology-based risk profiles.

label: PHOENIX trial
definition: A cohort of patients with non-germinal centre B-cell diffuse large B-cell lymphoma enrolled in the phase III PHOENIX trial of ibrutinib with R-CHOP chemotherapy, whose tumours were profiled by RNA sequencing and targeted panel sequencing.

label: Polish glioma cohort
definition: A cohort of Polish patients with gliomas of WHO grades II to IV whose tumours and matched blood were sequenced with a panel of cancer- and epigenetics-related genes to characterise somatic and germline variants.

label: Posthumous Evaluation of Advanced Cancer Environment
definition: A research autopsy programme in the United Kingdom in which patients with advanced cancer consent to post-mortem sampling of primary and metastatic tumours, enabling multi-region sequencing to decipher the evolution of metastasis and therapy resistance.

label: PRedicting Outcomes For Crohn's disease using a moLecular biomarker
definition: A cohort of adults with newly diagnosed active Crohn's disease enrolled in the multicentre, biomarker-stratified, randomised PROFILE trial in the United Kingdom, whose stool samples were sequenced to relate the gut microbiome to treatment response.

label: Pregnancy Outcome Prediction study
definition: A prospective cohort of 4,512 nulliparous women with viable singleton pregnancies recruited at the Rosie Hospital, Cambridge, United Kingdom, during 2008–2012 and followed with serial ultrasonography, blood sampling and placental collection to identify biomarkers of adverse pregnancy outcomes.

label: Premature Atherosclerosis Study pedigrees
definition: A collection of pedigrees with premature atherosclerosis from the Amsterdam Medical Center, exome sequenced to identify rare genetic variants contributing to cardiovascular disease.

label: PrevANZ trial
definition: A cohort of people with a first demyelinating event randomised in the phase IIb PrevANZ trial in Australia and New Zealand to daily oral vitamin D3 or placebo, with blood transcriptomes at baseline and 12 weeks to investigate prevention of multiple sclerosis.

label: Prevention and Incidence of Asthma and Mite Allergy
definition: A Dutch birth cohort of children born in 1996–1997 followed from pregnancy into adulthood to investigate the prevention and incidence of asthma and mite allergy, with nasal gene expression and epigenetic data collected in adolescence.

label: Princess Margaret Cancer Centre acute myeloid leukemia patient cohort
definition: A cohort of 81 acute myeloid leukaemia patients whose viably frozen samples from the Leukemia Tissue Bank at Princess Margaret Cancer Centre, Toronto, engraft in immunodeficient mice and were profiled by RNA sequencing.

label: Radar cohort
definition: A cohort of 110 children from 70 families whose fathers were exposed to ionizing radiation as radar technicians, whole-genome sequenced to look for transgenerational signatures of paternal radiation exposure.

label: Research on Obesity and Diabetes among African Migrants
definition: A cohort of Ghanaian adults living in rural and urban Ghana and in European cities, followed over time to unravel the causes of cardiovascular disease and its risk factors among African migrants in Europe and non-migrants in sub-Saharan Africa.

label: ROBUST trial
definition: A cohort of patients with newly diagnosed activated B-cell diffuse large B-cell lymphoma enrolled in the phase III ROBUST trial of lenalidomide with R-CHOP chemotherapy versus placebo, whose tumours were profiled by RNA and whole-genome sequencing.

label: SARS-CoV-2 Vaccine Response in Cancer trial
definition: A prospective multicentre cohort of patients with haematological malignancies and healthy controls recruited by the Istituto Romagnolo per lo Studio dei Tumori in Italy to investigate the immunological response to mRNA SARS-CoV-2 vaccines.

label: Schizophrenia Exome Sequencing Meta-analysis consortium
definition: An international consortium that meta-analyses exome sequences of schizophrenia cases and controls contributed by member studies to identify genes in which rare coding variants confer risk of schizophrenia.

label: Severe Childhood Onset Obesity Project
definition: A United Kingdom cohort of individuals of European ancestry with severe early-onset obesity, a subset of the Genetics of Obesity Study, used to identify common and rare variants contributing to severe obesity.

label: SG10K Pilot
definition: A collection of 4,810 Singapore Chinese, Malays and Indians whose whole genomes were sequenced in the pilot phase of the SG10K project, a precursor of PRECISE-SG100K, to characterise Asian genetic diversity and improve imputation in Asian populations.

label: STRAT-PARK
definition: A longitudinal cohort study in Norway that aims to stratify neurodegenerative parkinsonisms into biological subtypes using biomarkers, including mitochondrial function in muscle biopsies from people with Parkinson's disease and healthy controls.

label: STREP GENE
definition: A collection of survivors of invasive group A streptococcal disease in the United Kingdom, recruited through a patient group or identified from a tissue bank at Imperial College London and genotyped genome-wide to investigate host genetic susceptibility.

label: Stroke Investigative Research and Education Network
definition: An H3Africa case-control study of stroke in sub-Saharan Africa that recruits stroke cases and matched controls at hospital and community sites in Ghana and Nigeria to evaluate genetic and environmental risk factors for stroke in people of African ancestry.

label: Study Into Lean and Thin Subjects
definition: A cohort of about 1,600 persistently thin, healthy adults with a body mass index below 18 kg/m2 and no chronic disease or eating disorder, recruited through primary care in the United Kingdom from 2005 to investigate the genetic basis of thinness.

label: SweGen
definition: A whole-genome sequence resource of 1,000 individuals selected as a cross-section of the Swedish population, mostly from the Swedish Twin Registry with a smaller set from the Northern Sweden Population Health Study, providing a national reference of genetic variation.

label: Sys4MS cohort
definition: A prospective cohort of patients with multiple sclerosis recruited at European centres by the Sys4MS project, with clinical, imaging and omics data to develop systems medicine models of the disease.

label: Therapeutically Applicable Research to Generate Effective Treatments
definition: A National Cancer Institute initiative that assembles cohorts of children with hard-to-treat cancers, including leukaemias, neuroblastoma, Wilms tumour and osteosarcoma, for comprehensive molecular characterisation to accelerate the development of markers and therapies.

label: TRACERx
definition: A prospective cohort of patients with early-stage non-small cell lung cancer recruited across the United Kingdom, whose tumours are sampled in multiple regions before and through therapy to investigate intratumour heterogeneity and clonal evolution in relation to outcome.

label: TransplantLines
definition: A single-centre prospective cohort study and biobank at the University Medical Center Groningen, the Netherlands, of recipients of all types of solid organ transplant and of living organ donors, with gut microbiome characterisation linked to clinical phenotypes.

label: TrypanoGEN
definition: An H3Africa collection of cases, controls and latent infections from seven populations of Uganda, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Ivory Coast, Guinea, Cameroon and Zambia where trypanosomiasis is endemic, sequenced to discover genetic variants associated with responses to sleeping sickness infection.

label: Tumor Profiler
definition: An observational Swiss study that applied multi-omic and functional tumour profiling to samples from patients with metastatic melanoma, metastatic epithelial ovarian cancer and acute myeloid leukaemia to assess the value of in-depth profiling for clinical decision support.

label: Type 2 Diabetes Genetic Exploration by Next-generation sequencing in multi-Ethnic Samples
definition: A consortium of United States and United Kingdom groups that sequenced the exomes of 6,546 type 2 diabetes cases and 6,457 controls of African American, East Asian, South Asian, Hispanic and European ancestry, drawn from member cohorts, to assess common, low-frequency and rare variants in diabetes risk.

label: Uganda General Population Cohort
definition: A population-based cohort of about 6,400 individuals from a geographically defined rural community in south-west Uganda, established in 1989 and genotyped and sequenced by the African Partnership for Chronic Disease Research as the Uganda Genome Resource.

label: UK BHF CAD/MI cohort
definition: A British Heart Foundation collection of patients with coronary artery disease or myocardial infarction and a strong family history, whose early-onset cases were sequenced with the German MI cohort in the Cardiogenics re-sequencing study.

label: UK Blood Service Control Group
definition: A collection of blood donors recruited through the UK Blood Services as a population control set for the Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium and later genetic association studies.

label: UK10K
definition: A project that sequenced the genomes of 4,000 participants of the TwinsUK and ALSPAC cohorts and the exomes of 6,000 individuals selected for extreme phenotypes and rare diseases, to find low-frequency and rare variants contributing to disease in the United Kingdom.

label: UK10K Rare Neuromuscular Disorders cohort
definition: A collection of patients with rare neuromuscular disorders, contributed by Francesco Muntoni's group, that formed part of the rare disease arm of the UK10K project and was exome and genome sequenced to find causal variants.

label: University of Washington ovarian carcinoma cohort
definition: A cohort of 56 patients with primary, treatment-naive ovarian carcinoma at the University of Washington whose tumours were RNA sequenced to relate BRCA and immune configurations to response to platinum-based chemotherapy.

label: UPTIDER
definition: A monocentric post-mortem tissue donation programme at UZ Leuven, Belgium, in which women with metastatic breast cancer donate primary, metastatic and normal tissues after death for multi-region molecular profiling.

label: VIVO Biobank
definition: A United Kingdom biobank of pathological samples from over 600 patients with rhabdomyosarcoma and other childhood cancers, with detailed clinical annotation, supporting whole-genome and transcriptome sequencing to identify risk biomarkers.

label: West Coast Prostate Cancer Dream Team
definition: A cohort of patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer whose metastasis biopsies and plasma were collected by the Stand Up To Cancer and Prostate Cancer Foundation West Coast Dream Team at United States west coast centres for genome, methylome and transcriptome sequencing.

label: WTCCC case-control study for Ankylosing Spondylitis
definition: The Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium's collection of ankylosing spondylitis cases from the United Kingdom, analysed in a genome-wide case-control association study against the 1958 British Birth Cohort and UK Blood Service control collections.

label: WTCCC case-control study for Autoimmune Thyroid Disease
definition: The Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium's collection of autoimmune thyroid disease cases from the United Kingdom, analysed in a genome-wide case-control association study against the 1958 British Birth Cohort and UK Blood Service control collections.

label: WTCCC case-control study for Bipolar Disorder
definition: The Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium's collection of bipolar disorder cases from the United Kingdom, analysed in a genome-wide case-control association study against the 1958 British Birth Cohort and UK Blood Service control collections.

label: WTCCC case-control study for Breast cancer
definition: The Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium's collection of breast cancer cases from the United Kingdom, analysed in a genome-wide case-control association study against the 1958 British Birth Cohort and UK Blood Service control collections.

label: WTCCC case-control study for Coronary Artery Disease
definition: The Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium's collection of coronary artery disease cases from the United Kingdom, analysed in a genome-wide case-control association study against the 1958 British Birth Cohort and UK Blood Service control collections.

label: WTCCC case-control study for Hypertension
definition: The Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium's collection of hypertension cases from the United Kingdom, analysed in a genome-wide case-control association study against the 1958 British Birth Cohort and UK Blood Service control collections.

label: WTCCC case-control study for Inflammatory Bowel Disease
definition: The Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium's collection of inflammatory bowel disease cases from the United Kingdom, analysed in a genome-wide case-control association study against the 1958 British Birth Cohort and UK Blood Service control collections.

label: WTCCC case-control study for Multiple Sclerosis
definition: The Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium's collection of multiple sclerosis cases from the United Kingdom, analysed in a genome-wide case-control association study against the 1958 British Birth Cohort and UK Blood Service control collections.

label: WTCCC case-control study for Rheumatoid Arthritis
definition: The Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium's collection of rheumatoid arthritis cases from the United Kingdom, analysed in a genome-wide case-control association study against the 1958 British Birth Cohort and UK Blood Service control collections.

label: WTCCC case-control study for Tuberculosis
definition: The Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium's collection of tuberculosis cases and controls from Africa, analysed in a genome-wide case-control association study using African samples as controls.

label: WTCCC case-control study for Type 1 Diabetes
definition: The Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium's collection of type 1 diabetes cases from the United Kingdom, analysed in a genome-wide case-control association study against the 1958 British Birth Cohort and UK Blood Service control collections.

label: WTCCC case-control study for Type 2 Diabetes
definition: The Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium's collection of type 2 diabetes cases from the United Kingdom, analysed in a genome-wide case-control association study against the 1958 British Birth Cohort and UK Blood Service control collections.

label: Charles F. and Joanne Knight Alzheimer Disease Research Center
definition: A cohort of research volunteers recruited over more than 40 years by the Charles F. and Joanne Knight Alzheimer Disease Research Center at Washington University in St. Louis, United States, largely through its Memory and Aging Project and Memory Diagnostic Clinic, and followed with cognitive, neuropsychological, imaging, fluid biomarker, genomic and multi-omic assessments to study Alzheimer disease and related dementias.

label: Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative
definition: A multi-site longitudinal cohort of cognitively normal older adults and people with mild cognitive impairment or mild Alzheimer disease, recruited from 2004 at over 60 clinical sites in the United States and Canada by the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative, a public-private partnership, to evaluate neuroimaging, fluid biomarker and clinical measures of Alzheimer disease progression.

label: Dominantly Inherited Alzheimer Network
definition: An international longitudinal cohort of asymptomatic and symptomatic carriers of autosomal dominant Alzheimer disease mutations and their non-carrier family members, followed by a network of Alzheimer disease centres coordinated from Washington University in St. Louis with standard clinical, cognitive, neuroimaging and fluid biomarker protocols to determine the pathochronology of the disease.

label: Barcelona-1
definition: A longitudinal observational memory-clinic cohort of about 300 people at baseline, diagnosed with Alzheimer disease dementia, other dementias, mild cognitive impairment or subjective memory complaints, assembled at the Memory Disorders Unit of the University Hospital Mútua de Terrassa near Barcelona, Spain, with cerebrospinal fluid and amyloid PET biomarkers collected for selected participants.

label: Stockholm-Tartu Atherosclerosis Reverse Networks Engineering Task
definition: A cohort of patients with coronary artery disease undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting, with comparison patients undergoing other open-heart surgery, enrolled at the Department of Cardiac Surgery of Tartu University Hospital in Estonia, whose vascular and metabolic tissues and blood were genotyped, RNA-sequenced and proteomically profiled to study gene regulation underlying cardiometabolic disease.

label: Million Veteran Program
definition: An observational cohort and mega-biobank of veterans enrolled since 2011 at recruiting sites of the Department of Veterans Affairs health care system in the United States, combining questionnaires, electronic health records and blood samples for genomic testing to study genetic influences on health and disease.

label: Chinese Imaging Genetics study
definition: A cohort of healthy Chinese Han adults aged 18–30 years recruited at research centres in mainland Chinese cities by the Chinese Imaging Genetics (CHIMGEN) study, collecting genomic, neuroimaging, environmental and behavioural data to identify genetic and environmental factors associated with neuroimaging and behavioural phenotypes.

label: African American Study of Kidney Disease and Hypertension
definition: A cohort of African American adults aged 18–70 with hypertensive chronic kidney disease, enrolled at clinical centres across the United States in a randomized trial of antihypertensive drug regimens and blood-pressure goals (1995–2001) and then followed in the AASK Cohort Study to identify risk factors for progressive kidney disease.

label: Amsterdam Dementia Cohort
definition: A cohort of almost 6,000 patients who have visited the memory clinic of the Alzheimer Center at VU University Medical Center (Amsterdam UMC) in Amsterdam, the Netherlands, since 2000, followed in an ongoing observational study that combines patient care with research on early diagnosis, heterogeneity and vascular factors in dementia.

label: Protein Aggregation and Neurotransmitter Deficits Study
definition: A longitudinal cohort of people with Parkinson disease and healthy older controls studied by the Campbell Research Lab in the Section of Movement Disorders at Washington University in St. Louis, United States, assessed every two years with MRI, motor, gait and cognitive testing, optional lumbar puncture and clinical interview to understand the role of brain proteins and neurotransmitters in Parkinson disease symptoms compared with healthy aging.

label: Protein and Imaging Biomarkers of Parkinson Disease Study
definition: A longitudinal cohort of people with Parkinson disease and healthy older controls studied by the Campbell Research Lab in the Section of Movement Disorders at Washington University in St. Louis, United States, assessed every three years with MRI, motor, gait and cognitive testing, optional lumbar puncture, amyloid and cholinergic PET and clinical interview to relate clinical symptoms to brain changes in Parkinson disease compared with healthy aging.

label: BioBank Japan
definition: A patient-based biobank of about 200,000 people diagnosed with any of 47 common diseases, enrolled in 2003–2008 at 12 cooperative medical institutes across Japan by the BioBank Japan Project, with DNA, serum and annually collected clinical information to support genomic research and personalized medicine.

label: Age, Gene/Environment Susceptibility-Reykjavik Study
definition: A cohort of older men and women born in 1907–1935, drawn from the population-based Reykjavik Study followed in Iceland by the Icelandic Heart Association and re-examined from 2002 with detailed cardiovascular, neurocognitive, musculoskeletal and metabolic phenotypes to study genetic susceptibility and gene–environment interaction in disease and disability in old age.

label: Stanford Alzheimer's Disease Research Center
definition: A cohort of research participants followed by the Stanford Alzheimer's Disease Research Center, one of the US National Institutes of Health-funded Alzheimer's Disease Research Centers, whose clinical and research focus spans Alzheimer disease and Lewy body disorders, contributing cerebrospinal fluid proteomic and whole-genome sequence data to genetic studies.

label: Canadian Longitudinal Study on Aging
definition: A national stratified cohort of 51,338 women and men aged 45–85 years recruited in 2011–2015 from all 10 Canadian provinces, comprising a telephone-interviewed Tracking cohort and an in-person Comprehensive cohort providing physical assessments and blood and urine samples, assembled as a longitudinal research platform for studying health and aging.

label: Jackson Heart Study
definition: A community-based cohort of 5,302 African American adults, including a nested family cohort, enrolled from the three counties of the Jackson, Mississippi metropolitan area, with extensive medical, social, physical and biochemical measurements and genomic DNA, to study cardiovascular and related diseases in African Americans.

label: UK Biobank Pharma Proteomics Project
definition: A sub-cohort of 54,219 UK Biobank participants, mostly a random selection of baseline participants plus individuals chosen by consortium members and participants in the COVID-19 repeat-imaging study, whose plasma proteomes were profiled by the UK Biobank Pharma Proteomics Project, a precompetitive consortium of biopharmaceutical companies, to map genetic and health associations of circulating proteins.

label: Mass General Brigham Biobank
definition: A healthcare-based biobank of more than 140,000 consenting patients of the Mass General Brigham network in the Greater Boston area of Massachusetts, enrolled since 2010 at Massachusetts General Hospital, Brigham and Women’s Hospital and local sites, linking biological samples, genomic data and health records to study genetic and environmental influences on disease in clinical practice.

label: Cardiovascular Health Study
definition: A population-based longitudinal cohort of men and women aged 65 years and older sampled from Medicare eligibility lists in four US communities (Forsyth County, North Carolina; Sacramento County, California; Washington County, Maryland; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania) from 1989, with mostly Black participants added in 1992–1993, to identify factors related to the onset and course of coronary heart disease and stroke in older adults.

label: Framingham Heart Study
definition: A community-based, multi-generational cohort of residents of Framingham, Massachusetts, begun with the Original Cohort in 1948 and extended by the Offspring (1971), Third Generation (2002) and OMNI cohorts, examined every 2–4 years to define cardiovascular disease risk factors and, increasingly, the genetic and molecular epidemiology of a wide range of diseases.

label: Rhineland Study
definition: An ongoing population-based cohort of people aged 30 or above living in two geographically defined areas of Bonn, Germany, invited in random order by the German Centre for Neurodegenerative Diseases (DZNE) for deep phenotyping, imaging and omics studies of health and ageing.

label: European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition-Potsdam
definition: The German centre of the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition, a cohort of 27,548 adults from the general population around Potsdam in eastern Germany, mostly aged 35–65 at recruitment in 1994–1998, followed up prospectively to study diet, metabolism and chronic diseases such as type 2 diabetes and cancer.

label: Hispanic Community Health Study/Study of Latinos
definition: A multicentre community-based cohort of about 16,000 men and women aged 18–74 who self-identify as Hispanic or Latino, recruited from random samples of households in the Bronx, Chicago, Miami and San Diego in the United States, to study the prevalence of and risk factors for cardiovascular, pulmonary, metabolic and other chronic diseases.

label: Busselton Health Study
definition: A community-based longitudinal cohort of residents of the town and Shire of Busselton in south-western Western Australia, surveyed since 1966 and including related and unrelated individuals of predominantly European ancestry, whose 1994/95 follow-up provided blood samples for genetic studies of cardiovascular, respiratory and metabolic traits.

label: Swedish Infrastructure for Medical Population-Based Life-Course and Environmental Research
definition: A Swedish research infrastructure combining two large ongoing population-based cohorts, the Cohort of Swedish Men and the Swedish Mammography Cohort, whose randomly selected subsamples from Västmanland and Uppsala were clinically examined with genotyping and biosampling for life-course studies of health.

label: Swedish CArdioPulmonary bioImage Study
definition: A national multicentre cohort of about 30,000 Swedish men and women aged 50–64, characterised with imaging, large-scale omics and epidemiological data to improve risk prediction of cardiopulmonary diseases and study their mechanisms.

label: Malmö Offspring Study
definition: A family cohort of about 4,700 adults aged 18–71, the children and grandchildren of Malmö Diet and Cancer Study participants in Malmö, Sweden, examined from 2013 with genotyping, cardiovascular, respiratory, metabolic, cognitive, dietary and microbiota phenotyping to study family traits of chronic disease across three generations.

label: Metabolic Syndrome in Men Study
definition: A population-based cohort of 10,197 middle-aged and older Finnish men from a single site in north-eastern Finland, examined in 2005–2010 with detailed metabolic phenotyping, oral glucose tolerance tests, metabolomics and extensive genotyping and sequencing, and followed up to study nongenetic and genetic risk factors for type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease.

label: Qatar Genome Program
definition: A national whole-genome sequencing programme of the Qatar Foundation that sequences volunteers from the Qatar Biobank and combines their genomes with the biobank's phenotype data to study the Qatari and wider Arab and Middle Eastern populations at the molecular level.

label: Trøndelag Health Study
definition: A population-based cohort of the adult population of Trøndelag County, Norway, in which all residents of Nord-Trøndelag aged 20 or over have been invited to repeated surveys since 1984–86, extended to Sør-Trøndelag in 2017–19, collecting questionnaires, interviews, clinical examinations, laboratory measurements and biological samples on a broad range of health topics.

label: Simons Foundation Powering Autism Research for Knowledge
definition: A cohort of individuals with a professional diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder living in the United States, together with their parents and unaffected siblings, recruited online by the Simons Foundation Autism Research Initiative (SFARI) to collect genomic, medical and longitudinal behavioural data and to connect participants with researchers.

label: Chronic Renal Insufficiency Cohort Study
definition: A cohort of racially and ethnically diverse adults aged 21 to 74 with chronic kidney disease, recruited at seven clinical centres in the United States from 2003 and followed with annual clinical evaluations and biospecimen collection to examine risk factors for the progression of chronic kidney disease and cardiovascular disease.

label: Systematic and Combined Analysis of Olink Proteins
definition: A consortium of principal investigators of cohort studies from the general population, clinical trials and disease-specific patient collections that have Olink proteomics and genome-wide genotyping data, combining summary-level data to discover and follow up genetic associations with plasma protein levels (pQTLs) and identify causal protein biomarkers of disease.

label: China Medical University Hospital Biobank
definition: A hospital-based cohort of about 413,000 patients of China Medical University Hospital and its affiliated branches in Taichung, Taiwan, genotyped on a custom Taiwan Precision Medicine array and linked to electronic medical records from 2003 to 2021 (the HiGenome resource), assembled for genome-wide, phenome-wide and polygenic risk score studies in the Taiwanese Han population.

label: Religious Orders Study and Rush Memory and Aging Project
definition: A pair of harmonized longitudinal clinical-pathologic cohort studies of aging and Alzheimer's disease run at Rush University, the Religious Orders Study (from 1994, nuns, priests and brothers from across the United States) and the Rush Memory and Aging Project (from 1997, lay persons from northeastern Illinois), whose older participants enrol without dementia and agree to annual clinical evaluations and organ donation.

label: Mayo Clinic Biobank
definition: A clinic-based prospective cohort of about 57,000 adult Mayo Clinic patients who are US residents, enrolled at Rochester, Minnesota, Jacksonville, Florida and La Crosse, Wisconsin, established to supply control groups for case-control studies, form a prospective cohort for common outcomes and support electronic health record and genotype-driven research.

label: HOLBAEK Study
definition: A cohort of Danish children and adolescents combining an obesity clinic cohort treated at the Children's Obesity Clinic, Copenhagen University Hospital Holbæk, and a population-based cohort recruited from schools in 11 municipalities in Zealand, enrolled between 2009 and 2019 with genotyping and deep cardiometabolic phenotyping to study the causes and consequences of childhood obesity.

label: FinnGen
definition: A public–private partnership research project in Finland that combines genotype data from newly collected and legacy samples of about 500,000 participants of a nationwide network of Finnish biobanks with digital health data from national health registers, to provide genetic insights into disease in an isolated population enriched for low-frequency variants.

label: NIHR BioResource Rare Diseases Study
definition: A cohort of patients with rare diseases or extreme measurements of quantitative traits, their affected relatives and controls, enrolled mainly at National Health Service hospitals in the United Kingdom between 2012 and 2017 under the coordination of the NIHR BioResource at the University of Cambridge, whose whole genomes were sequenced to provide genetic diagnoses and discover aetiological variants within routine healthcare.

label: Australian Imaging, Biomarker & Lifestyle Flagship Study of Ageing
definition: A longitudinal cohort of volunteers aged over 60 in Australia, including people with Alzheimer's disease, mild cognitive impairment and healthy controls, recruited at centres in Perth and Melbourne and reassessed at 18-month intervals with cognitive testing, blood biomarkers, lifestyle questionnaires and amyloid PET and MRI imaging to study predictors of Alzheimer's disease and cognitive decline.

label: PopGen Biobank
definition: A population-based biobank in the most northern part of Germany, run from Kiel University, that recruits patients through complete ascertainment in a geographically confined area together with population controls, covering cardiovascular, neuropsychiatric and environmental diseases, to estimate population-specific genotypic risks for complex diseases.

label: Diabetic Nephropathy Cohort
definition: A cohort of outpatients with type 2 diabetes of Chinese, Malay and Asian Indian ancestry recruited from the diabetes centre of a regional hospital in Singapore between 2004 and 2015 to study the development and progression of diabetic nephropathy and of major cardiovascular disease.

label: Singapore Study of Macro-Angiopathy and Micro-Vascular Reactivity in Type 2 Diabetes
definition: A prospective cohort of adults with type 2 diabetes of Chinese, Malay, Indian and other ancestry recruited in 2011–2014 from a public hospital and primary care polyclinics in northern Singapore and followed in three-yearly waves to study risk factors for vascular function and diabetes-related complications such as kidney disease, retinopathy and cognitive dysfunction.

label: Women's Health Initiative
definition: A cohort of postmenopausal women aged 50–79 enrolled from 1993 at 40 clinical centres across the United States into a clinical trial of dietary modification, hormone therapy and calcium and vitamin D supplementation or into a parallel observational study, followed to study the prevention of cancer, cardiovascular disease and osteoporotic fractures.

label: SHIP-TREND
definition: A population-based cohort of adults aged 20–79 sampled from Western Pomerania, a rural region of north-eastern Germany, and recruited in 2008–2012 as the second, independent cohort of the Study of Health in Pomerania, examined at baseline and followed up to study health, disease and their risk factors.

label: Korean Genome and Epidemiology Study
definition: A consortium of six Korean cohorts, population-based and gene–environment model studies initiated from 2001 with about 245,000 participants, investigating the genetic and environmental determinants of health, disease and ageing in the Korean population.

label: Netherlands Epidemiology of Obesity Study
definition: A population-based prospective cohort of 6,673 men and women aged 45–65 from the greater area of Leiden, the Netherlands, oversampling people with overweight or obesity, recruited in 2008–2012 for extensive phenotyping to investigate the pathways that lead to obesity-related diseases.

label: Wisconsin Registry for Alzheimer's Prevention
definition: A longitudinal observational cohort of middle-aged adults enriched for persons with a parental history of probable Alzheimer disease dementia, enrolled since 2001 at the University of Wisconsin–Madison, United States, and followed with serial cognitive assessments, medical and lifestyle histories, laboratory tests, genetics and linked imaging and cerebrospinal fluid studies to study the early course of Alzheimer disease.

label: Wisconsin Alzheimer's Disease Research Center
definition: A longitudinal cohort of middle-aged and older adults recruited into diagnostic and risk subgroups by the Wisconsin Alzheimer's Disease Research Center at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, United States, to study memory, aging and Alzheimer disease, with cerebrospinal fluid biomarker, metabolomic and genotype data.

label: Food Chain Plus
definition: A cohort of 1,795 adults aged 18–83 from the Kiel region of northern Germany, enrolled in 2011–2014 at random via residents' registration offices and via the Obesity Outpatient Centre of the University Medical Center Schleswig-Holstein, for population-based research on metabolic inflammation with multi-omics, nutrition and follow-up every five years.

label: Amish Complex Disease Research Program
definition: A research programme of the University of Maryland studying adults of the Old Order Amish founder population of Lancaster County, Pennsylvania, of whom over 7,000 have taken part in one or more of its studies of the genetics of complex diseases.

label: BioVU
definition: A biobank of Vanderbilt University Medical Center patients in Nashville, Tennessee, whose DNA, extracted from discarded clinical blood samples under an opt-out model, is linked to a de-identified copy of their electronic medical records (the synthetic derivative) for genomic and personalised-medicine research.

label: Southall and Brent Revisited
definition: A tri-ethnic longitudinal cohort of people of European, South Asian and African Caribbean ethnicity living in West and North London, United Kingdom, set up in 1988 to examine ethnic differences in chronic disease.

label: Gut-and-Liver Axis in Alcoholic Liver Fibrosis
definition: A cohort of consecutively recruited patients with a history of harmful drinking and early, asymptomatic alcohol-related liver disease, together with matched healthy participants, recruited in the Region of Southern Denmark by the EU Horizon 2020 GALAXY consortium to study the gut–liver axis and non-invasive markers of alcohol-related liver fibrosis.

label: Cardiovascular Risk in Young Finns Study
definition: A population-based cohort of 3,596 randomly selected Finnish children and adolescents aged 3–18 years at baseline in 1980, followed into adulthood for over three decades to study how cardiovascular risk factors in childhood relate to preclinical markers of cardiovascular disease in adulthood.

label: Study of Colorectal Cancer in Scotland
definition: A population-based case–control study of colorectal cancer in Scotland, recruiting colorectal cancer cases and population controls since 1999, whose genotyped cases are followed for survival, used to study genetic susceptibility to colorectal cancer and its outcomes.

label: China Kadoorie Biobank
definition: A population-based prospective cohort of more than 512,000 adults recruited in 2004–2008 from 10 geographically diverse regions of China, with baseline questionnaires and physical measurements, periodic resurveys, genome-wide genotyping of over 100,000 participants and electronic linkage to death, disease and health-insurance records, supporting studies of disease risk factors, genetics and drug targets.

label: All of Us Research Program
definition: A national research cohort led by the National Institutes of Health that aims to enrol at least one million diverse adults in the United States, most from groups historically under-represented in biomedical research, through more than 340 recruitment sites, collecting health questionnaires, electronic health records, physical measurements, digital health data and biospecimens to advance precision medicine.

label: BioMe Biobank
definition: An electronic health record-linked biobank founded in 2007 at the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai that enrols participants non-selectively from the Mount Sinai Health System in New York City, comprising about 60,000 ancestrally diverse participants with genotype and sequence data for genetic and clinical research.

label: Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults Study
definition: A prospective cohort of young adults aged 18–30 years, balanced by sex and by Black and White race, recruited in 1985–1986 at four field centres in Birmingham, Alabama, Chicago, Illinois, Minneapolis, Minnesota and Oakland, California, and followed with repeated examinations into midlife to study the development of cardiovascular risk factors and disease.

label: Health for Life in Singapore
definition: A prospective population-based cohort of 10,004 men and women of Chinese, Indian or Malay background aged 30–84, recruited from the Singapore general population in 2018–2022 by Nanyang Technological University, with behavioural, phenotypic and multi-omic measurements and health-record linkage for precision-medicine research in Asian populations.

label: Cleveland Family Study
definition: A family-based longitudinal cohort of index probands with laboratory-confirmed obstructive sleep apnoea, their relatives, and neighbourhood control families recruited from the Cleveland metropolitan area, Ohio, with four examinations between 1990 and 2006, designed to study the familial and genetic basis of sleep-disordered breathing.

label: deCODE genetics Icelandic cohort
definition: A population sample of Icelanders recruited through the disease-specific and general-population research projects of deCODE genetics in Reykjavik, Iceland, including the deCODE Health Study, whose chip genotypes and whole-genome sequences, combined with the nationwide Icelandic genealogy, are used for genome-wide association studies of diseases and other traits.

label: PainOMICS Retrospective Study
definition: A retrospective, multicentre case–control study of adults with chronic low back pain and controls, recruited at clinical pain centres in Italy, Croatia, Belgium, Australia and the United States within the European Union FP7-funded PainOMICS project, collecting clinical data and blood samples for genome-wide association, glycomics and activomics analyses of chronic low back pain.

label: The Pomak cohort
definition: A population-based cohort from a set of religiously and geographically isolated mountainous Pomak villages in northern Greece, part of the Hellenic Isolated Cohorts (HELIC), whose whole-genome sequence and serum protein data are used to study genetic variation and complex traits in an isolated population.

label: Genetic Epidemiology Research on Adult Health and Aging
definition: A multi-ethnic cohort of over 100,000 adult members of the Kaiser Permanente Northern California health plan who consented to the Research Program on Genes, Environment and Health (RPGEH), linking survey data, saliva-derived DNA with genome-wide genotypes and telomere length, and electronic health records for research on the genetic and environmental determinants of common age-related diseases.

label: Correlated Expression and Disease Association Research
definition: A cohort of about 320 healthy adult Europeans visiting the Academic Hospital of the University of Liège, Belgium, as part of a national colon-cancer screening campaign, from whom peripheral blood and intestinal biopsies were collected to generate transcriptomes of circulating immune cell types and gut tissues for expression quantitative trait locus analysis of inflammatory bowel disease risk loci.

label: Generation Scotland: Scottish Family Health Study
definition: A family-based population cohort of 24,084 adults recruited throughout Scotland in 2006–2011 by Generation Scotland, a multi-institutional collaboration of universities and the NHS, who were extensively phenotyped and genotyped to study the genetics of common health conditions such as heart disease, stroke and depression.

label: Genetic Epidemiology Network of Arteriopathy
definition: A community-based family study of hypertensive sibships, recruited from 1996 among non-Hispanic Black adults in Jackson, Mississippi, non-Hispanic white adults in Rochester, Minnesota and (initially) Hispanic adults in Starr County, Texas, to identify genes influencing blood pressure and hypertensive target-organ damage.

label: Northern Finland Birth Cohorts
definition: A longitudinal research programme of the University of Oulu comprising two general-population birth cohorts from the two northernmost provinces of Finland, Oulu and Lapland, the Northern Finland Birth Cohort 1966 (NFBC1966) and 1986 (NFBC1986), whose members have been followed since the fetal period to study health and well-being.

label: Taiwan Biobank
definition: An ongoing prospective population biobank of more than 150,000 predominantly Han Chinese volunteers aged 20-70 recruited across Taiwan, with questionnaire, physical-measurement, biomarker and genome-wide genetic data and linkage to national health insurance records, built as a resource for biomedical and public health research in East Asia.

label: GeneRISK study
definition: A prospective cohort of about 7,300 adults aged 45-66 recruited in southern Finland in 2015-2017 (from the Kymenlaakso population register, occupational health care customers in Helsinki and Turku, and blood donors) to assess the impact of communicating genetic risk information for cardiovascular disease to participants.

label: Healthy Aging in Neighborhoods of Diversity across the Life Span
definition: A community-based prospective longitudinal study of 3,722 socioeconomically diverse African American and white adults aged 30-64 recruited in Baltimore, Maryland, examining how race, socioeconomic status, sex and age influence health and ageing.

label: Mount Sinai Crohn's and Colitis Registry
definition: A cross-sectional cohort of about 1,200 adults with Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis and non-IBD controls, prospectively recruited at endoscopy visits to the outpatient and endoscopy units of the Mount Sinai Hospital between December 2013 and September 2016, with intestinal biopsies, blood and genotype data for molecular studies of inflammatory bowel disease.

label: Netherlands Study of Depression and Anxiety
definition: A multi-site naturalistic longitudinal cohort of 2,981 adults aged 18-65 with current or lifetime depressive or anxiety disorders, people at risk and healthy controls, recruited in the general population, general practices and mental health organisations, to describe the long-term course and consequences of depressive and anxiety disorders and integrate biological and psychosocial predictors.

label: Health, Aging and Body Composition Study
definition: A prospective cohort of 3,075 community-dwelling Black and white adults aged 70-79, recruited from 1997 from white Medicare beneficiaries and all eligible Black residents in and around Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania and Memphis, Tennessee, and followed for about 17 years to study body composition, functional decline and disease in older age.

label: Michigan Genomics Initiative
definition: A single-health-system biobank of more than 91,000 adult patients recruited mainly during surgical encounters at Michigan Medicine, the University of Michigan health system, linking genotypes to electronic health records for disease genetics research.

label: Immune and Metabolic Markers during Pregnancy and Child Development Study
definition: A case-control study of mothers and children born at Kaiser Permanente Northern California from January 2011 to January 2016, oversampling children later diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder or other developmental delay alongside general-population controls, with maternal first- and second-trimester blood samples from the RPGEH pregnancy cohort, to study maternal immune and metabolic markers and child neurodevelopment.

label: Cohorts for Heart and Aging Research in Genomic Epidemiology Consortium
definition: A consortium of large prospective population-based cohort studies from the United States and Europe, founded with the Age, Gene/Environment Susceptibility-Reykjavik Study, the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities Study, the Cardiovascular Health Study, the Framingham Heart Study and the Rotterdam Study, formed to facilitate genome-wide association meta-analyses and replication across cohorts with similarly measured phenotypes.

label: Helsinki Birth Cohort Study
definition: A birth cohort of the 13,345 singletons born in one of the two maternity hospitals in Helsinki, Finland, between 1934 and 1944, followed up in later life to study how early life shapes adult health.

label: Generation R Study
definition: A population-based prospective cohort from fetal life onwards of 9,778 mothers with delivery dates from April 2002 to January 2006 in Rotterdam, the Netherlands, and their children, designed to identify early environmental and genetic causes of normal and abnormal growth, development and health.

label: 500 Functional Genomics
definition: A cohort of about 500 healthy adult volunteers of Western European ancestry recruited at Radboud University Medical Center in Nijmegen, the Netherlands, in 2013–2014 within the Human Functional Genomics Project, to study how genetic, environmental, host and microbiome factors shape individual cytokine and immune responses.

label: MyCode Community Health Initiative
definition: A biobank cohort of patients of Geisinger Health System, an integrated health system in central and eastern Pennsylvania, United States, who since 2007 have given opt-in consent to link their samples to electronic health record data for broad research use, with genotype and exome sequence data generated in collaboration with the Regeneron Genetics Center.

label: 23andMe research cohort
definition: A cohort of customers of 23andMe, Inc., a direct-to-consumer genetics company, who have been genotyped and have consented to take part in online research, answering web-based questionnaires under an IRB-approved protocol, whose genotype and self-reported data are used for genome-wide association studies.

label: LIFE-Adult-Study
definition: A population-based cohort of 10,000 randomly selected adults, mainly aged 40–79, from the city of Leipzig in eastern Germany, examined in 2011–2014 by the Leipzig Research Centre for Civilization Diseases (LIFE) with deep phenotyping to study the prevalence, early markers, genetic predispositions and lifestyle factors of major civilization diseases.

label: Red Blood Cell-Omics Study
definition: A cohort of more than 12,000 volunteer blood donors of diverse ancestry enrolled at four blood centres across the United States within the NHLBI-funded Recipient Epidemiology and Donor Evaluation Study (REDS-III), to study how donor genetics and biology affect the storage quality and haemolysis of donated red blood cells.

label: Corogene Study
definition: A prospective cohort of consecutive Finnish patients referred for coronary angiography at Helsinki University Central Hospital in 2006–2008, assembled to study the genetic predisposition to coronary heart disease; its acute coronary syndrome cases, with controls sampled from FINRISK, form a genotyped case-control sample.

label: Health 2000 GenMets Study
definition: A case-control sub-cohort of the Finnish Health 2000 survey, collected in 2000–2001, comprising participants with metabolic syndrome and matched controls, genotyped to study the genetics of metabolic syndrome and related traits.

label: Qatar Metabolomics Study on Diabetes
definition: A cross-sectional case–control study of 374 people with and without type 2 diabetes, of Arab and Asian descent, enrolled in February–June 2012 at the Dermatology Department of Hamad Medical Corporation in Doha, Qatar, with metabolomic profiling of saliva, blood plasma and urine to study metabolic dysregulation in diabetes.

label: Genetic Study of Atherosclerosis Risk
definition: A prospective family-based cohort, begun in 1983 at Johns Hopkins, of European American and African American families of probands with premature coronary disease identified in Baltimore-area hospitals, studied to determine the environmental, phenotypic and genetic causes of premature cardiovascular disease, including platelet response to a two-week aspirin trial.

label: Nurses' Health Study
definition: A prospective cohort of 121,700 female registered nurses in the United States aged 30–55 when enrolled through a baseline questionnaire in 1976, followed by repeated questionnaires and biospecimen collection to study lifestyle and other risk factors for major chronic diseases in women.

label: Penn Medicine BioBank
definition: An electronic health record-linked biobank cohort of more than 170,000 patients of the University of Pennsylvania Health System (Penn Medicine), about 30% of non-European ancestry, who consented to link their health records to genomic and biomarker data and to recontact, for genomic discovery and precision medicine research.

label: Epidemiological Investigation of Rheumatoid Arthritis
definition: A population-based case-control study established in Sweden in 1996, enrolling incident rheumatoid arthritis cases (now more than 5000) from the middle and southern regions of Sweden together with population controls, used to study genetic risk factors for rheumatoid arthritis and its ACPA-defined subsets and environmental factors such as cigarette smoking.

label: Ludwigshafen Risk and Cardiovascular Health Study
definition: A prospective cohort of 3,316 patients of German ancestry hospitalised for coronary angiography in Ludwigshafen, Germany, between 1997 and 2000, with and without cardiovascular disease, assembled to investigate genetic and environmental risk factors for cardiovascular diseases.

label: Diabetes Heart Study
definition: A family-based cohort of European American and African American siblings concordant for type 2 diabetes, and their unaffected relatives, recruited from internal medicine and endocrinology clinics in western North Carolina, United States, to study genetic and epidemiological contributions to diabetic heart disease and subclinical cardiovascular disease.

label: Genetics of Personality Consortium
definition: A consortium of about 30 cohorts with genome-wide genotype and personality data, which harmonized personality measures across inventories in more than 63,000 participants for genome-wide association meta-analyses of personality traits such as neuroticism and their relation to major depressive disorder.

label: Genetic Risk Assessment for Chinese Eaglet-T1D
definition: A case–control collection of children with type 1 diabetes and controls from multiple paediatric centres in China, used to validate polygenic risk scores for type 1 diabetes in an East Asian population.

label: Academic Medical Center Amsterdam Premature Atherosclerosis Study
definition: A prospective cohort of patients of the Academic Medical Center, Amsterdam, with symptomatic coronary artery disease (myocardial infarction, coronary revascularization or at least 70% stenosis of a major epicardial artery) before the age of 51, used in genetic studies of premature atherosclerosis and coronary artery disease.

label: Bogalusa Heart Study
definition: A long-term community-based cohort of Black and white children and adolescents in the rural biracial community of Bogalusa, Louisiana, United States, begun in 1972 by an NHLBI-funded research centre to study cardiovascular risk factors from early life and followed into adulthood.

label: Cleveland Family Speech and Reading Study
definition: A family-based longitudinal cohort of children with speech sound disorder of unknown cause and their siblings, ascertained through probands referred by speech-language pathologists in the Cleveland area of Ohio, United States, and followed for about 25 years to study long-term speech, language and literacy outcomes and their genetic basis.

label: Genetics of Opioid Addiction Consortium
definition: A consortium of investigators attending the National Institute on Drug Abuse Genetics and Epigenetics Cross-cutting Research Team meetings, pooling genome-wide association data on opioid addiction from ten independent cohorts, including Yale-Penn, the Vancouver Injection Drug Users Study, the Urban Health Study, COGA, deCODE and the Comorbidity and Trauma Study, to study the genetics of opioid addiction.

label: Genetics of Opioid Addiction Study
definition: A prospective cohort of adults with opioid use disorder receiving treatment at Canadian Addiction Treatment Centre clinics across Ontario, Canada, recruited in 2013–2016 in collaboration with McMaster University to identify factors, including genetic risk factors, associated with opioid use and treatment outcomes.

label: deCODE Health Study
definition: A general-population sample of Icelanders, enriched for carriers of rare and potentially high-impact mutations, comprehensively phenotyped by deCODE genetics in Iceland (e.g. audiometry, speech recordings, DXA body composition, plasma proteomics) and combined with the Icelandic genotype and sequence data for genetic association studies.

label: Qatar Biobank
definition: A population-based prospective cohort of adult Qatari nationals and long-term residents (living in Qatar for at least 15 years), recruited by the Qatar Biobank from December 2012 with extensive lifestyle, clinical, imaging and biological-sample data and long-term follow-up, to study the causes, progression and burden of disease in the Qatari population.

label: Reykjavik Study
definition: A population-based cohort of men born 1907–1934 and women born 1908–1935, randomly selected from residents of the Reykjavik area, examined at the Heart Preventive Clinic in Reykjavik from 1967 and followed since in Iceland by the Icelandic Heart Association, to study cardiovascular disease and its risk factors.

label: Human Functional Genomics Project
definition: A research programme based at Radboud University Medical Center in Nijmegen, the Netherlands, that collects distinct cohorts of healthy volunteers and patients (among them 500FG, 200FG, 300BCG, 300OB, 300DM and 2000HIV) profiled with genetic, immunological and other omics data, to identify the genetic and non-genetic determinants of human immune and cytokine responses.

label: Recipient Epidemiology and Donor Evaluation Study-III
definition: A seven-year multicentre transfusion-medicine research programme launched in 2011 by the US National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute, with a domestic component of four blood centres and 12 hospitals and international programmes in Brazil, China and South Africa, which built linked donor, donation and transfusion-recipient databases and ran more than 25 focused studies of blood donors and recipients, such as RBC-Omics and the Brazil sickle cell disease cohort.

label: Research Program on Genes, Environment and Health
definition: A research resource developed by the Kaiser Permanente Northern California Division of Research from consenting members of the KPNC health plan, linking surveys, biospecimens and electronic health records and including the Genetic Epidemiology Research on Adult Health and Aging cohort and a pregnancy cohort, for research on the genetic and environmental determinants of common, age-related complex health conditions.

label: Africa America Diabetes Mellitus Study
definition: A genetic epidemiology study of type 2 diabetes begun in 1997 as a collaboration of West African and US investigators, enrolling affected sib-pairs with type 2 diabetes and unaffected controls in Ghana and Nigeria and later participants in Eldoret, Kenya, to map type 2 diabetes susceptibility genes in the West African ancestral populations of African Americans.

label: Danish Blood Donor Study
definition: An ongoing nationwide prospective cohort of blood donors aged 18-70 at inclusion, recruited at Danish blood donation facilities since 2010 (all facilities in Denmark by 2015), with questionnaires, plasma samples, genotyping and linkage to national health registries for research on donor health and general public health.

label: Howard University Family Study
definition: A population-based family study of African Americans from the Washington, DC metropolitan area, enrolling randomly ascertained families and unrelated individuals through Howard University without selection on any phenotype, to study the genetic and environmental basis of common complex diseases including hypertension, obesity and type 2 diabetes.

label: Stabilization of Atherosclerotic Plaque by Initiation of Darapladib Therapy Trial
definition: An international randomized, placebo-controlled trial of darapladib, a lipoprotein-associated phospholipase A2 inhibitor, in 15,828 patients with chronic coronary heart disease recruited at 663 centers in 39 countries from December 2008 to April 2010 and sponsored by GlaxoSmithKline, whose baseline plasma biobank has been used for biomarker, proteomic and genetic studies of cardiovascular outcomes.

label: Swedish BioFINDER Study
definition: A prospective, longitudinal cohort of cognitively unimpaired older adults and patients with mild cognitive impairment, dementias and parkinsonian disorders, recruited from 2009 to 2014 at three neurology and memory clinics in southern Sweden and studied with cerebrospinal fluid, plasma, imaging and genetic data to find biomarkers for early and reliable diagnosis of neurodegenerative disease.

label: CROATIA-Vis Study
definition: A population-based cohort of 1,008 adult Croatians aged 18-93 from the isolated villages of Vis and Komiza on the Dalmatian island of Vis, Croatia, recruited in 2003 and 2004, genotyped and richly phenotyped for genetic studies of complex traits in an isolated population.

label: National Alzheimer's Coordinating Center
definition: A US data resource, founded in 1999 and funded by the National Institute on Aging, that combines the standardized longitudinal clinical (Uniform Data Set), neuropathology, imaging, biomarker and genetic data of participants of the NIA-funded Alzheimer's Disease Research Centers, more than 56,000 people from over 42 centers, for research on Alzheimer disease and related dementias.

label: Singapore Prospective Study Program
definition: A population-based study of diabetes and cardiovascular disease in Singapore that re-visited, between 2003 and 2007, Chinese, Malay and Asian-Indian adults randomly sampled for four earlier cross-sectional studies (the Thyroid and Heart Study, the 1992 and 1998 National Health Surveys and the National University of Singapore Heart Study), with questionnaires and clinical examinations.

label: Colorado Center for Personalized Medicine Biobank
definition: An electronic health record-linked biobank jointly developed by the University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus and UCHealth, enrolling adult UCHealth patients since September 2015 (more than 200,000 participants by 2022, mostly from the Rocky Mountain region), as a dual-purpose resource for genomic research and for returning clinical genetic results to participants.

label: Adult Changes in Thought Study
definition: A population-based prospective cohort of dementia-free adults aged 65 and older enrolled since 1994 from the membership of Kaiser Permanente Washington (formerly Group Health Cooperative) in the Seattle area, United States, and followed longitudinally to identify risk and preventive factors for dementia, with brain autopsy, genetic and abstracted medical-record data.

label: Hypertension Genetic Epidemiology Network
definition: A family study of the NHLBI Family Blood Pressure Program that from 1995 to 2000 recruited African American and white sibships with two or more members with hypertension diagnosed before age 60, with their untreated adult offspring and random population samples, at centres in Birmingham (Alabama), Forsyth County (North Carolina), Framingham (Massachusetts), Minneapolis (Minnesota) and Salt Lake City (Utah), to identify genes promoting hypertension.

label: Prostate, Lung, Colorectal, and Ovarian Cancer Screening Trial
definition: A multicentre randomized cancer screening trial of about 155,000 men and women aged 55–74, enrolled from 1993 to 2001 at ten screening centres across the United States under the National Cancer Institute, testing whether screening reduces mortality from prostate, lung, colorectal and ovarian cancer, with participants followed for cancer incidence and death.

label: Korean Cancer Prevention Study-II Biobank
definition: A prospective population-based biobank cohort of 156,701 Korean adults aged 20–85 recruited in 2004–2013 at 18 health promotion centres across Korea during routine health examinations, genotyped and followed through national mortality, cancer registry and health insurance records, to study cancer, cardiovascular and other chronic diseases and their metabolic risk factors.

label: Leipzig Research Center for Civilization Diseases-Heart Study
definition: A hospital-based cohort of patients with suspected stable coronary artery disease, acute myocardial infarction or known left main coronary artery disease undergoing coronary angiography at the Heart Center Leipzig, Germany, recruited from December 2006 by Leipzig University and its Leipzig Research Center for Civilization Diseases (LIFE) as a biobank and database for studying clinical, metabolic, cellular and genetic factors of atherosclerosis and coronary artery disease.

label: Bandim Health Project
definition: A health and demographic surveillance system in Guinea-Bissau, run by the Bandim Health Project with Statens Serum Institut, that since 1989-1990 has followed the women and children under five of 182 randomly selected clusters across the country through household visits, to study health interventions, the non-specific effects of vaccines and child mortality, and that hosts randomised vaccine trials.

label: Center for Applied Genomics Biobank
definition: A paediatric biobank of the Center for Applied Genomics at Children's Hospital of Philadelphia, recruiting children at the hospital since 2006 with broad consent for research use of their samples and electronic health records (about 85,000 juvenile subjects of diverse ancestries by 2025), used for genome-wide and phenome-wide studies of childhood disease.

label: Danish Twin Registry
definition: A nationwide population-based register of more than 175,000 Danish twins from birth cohorts 1870 to 2009, established in the 1950s, that combines repeated surveys, in-person assessments, a biobank and linkage to Danish national registers, for studies of genetic and environmental influences on health, disease and ageing.

label: Electronic Medical Records and Genomics Network
definition: A National Human Genome Research Institute-funded consortium, established in 2007, of US academic and integrated health systems, each with its own biorepository linking DNA samples to electronic medical records, which pooled its sites' data into a network-wide genome-wide dataset of about 105,000 participants for genomic discovery and later sequenced about 25,000 participants to study the return of genomic results.

label: Sorbs Study
definition: A volunteer-based cohort of about 1,000 adults from the self-contained population of Sorbs in eastern Germany, recruited and extensively metabolically phenotyped by the University of Leipzig in 2005–2007 for genome-wide studies of metabolic, anthropometric and other quantitative traits.

label: Dose-Responses to Exercise Training
definition: A four-year randomised controlled trial of resistance and aerobic exercise and dietary interventions in a population-based random sample of men and women aged 55-74 years living in Kuopio, Finland, drawn from the national population registry, of whom 1,479 attended baseline examinations in 2005-2006, to study the health effects of regular physical exercise and a healthy diet in middle-aged and older people.

label: Genetics of Lipid-Lowering Drugs and Diet Network
definition: A family intervention study of the NHLBI Programs in Gene by Environment Interaction, of 1,048 white participants in 184 three-generation pedigrees previously screened at the Minnesota and Utah centres of the NHLBI Family Heart Study, who took a standardised high-fat meal challenge and three weeks of fenofibrate treatment, to study genetic determinants of the lipid response to diet and lipid-lowering drugs.

label: Study of Women's Health Across the Nation
definition: A multi-site, multiethnic, community-based longitudinal cohort of 3,302 women aged 42–52 enrolled in 1996–1997 at seven US sites (Boston, Chicago, Detroit, Los Angeles, Pittsburgh, Oakland and Newark) and followed about yearly to study how women's physical, biological, psychological and social health in midlife affects health during ageing.

label: Finnish Diabetic Nephropathy Study
definition: An ongoing nationwide multicentre study in Finland, run since 1997 from the Folkhälsan Research Center and the University of Helsinki, of over 5,000 adults with type 1 diabetes enrolled and clinically characterised at study centres across the country to identify factors leading to diabetic nephropathy and other diabetic complications.

label: IMAGEN study
definition: A longitudinal multicentre genetic-neuroimaging cohort of about 2,000 healthy 14-year-old adolescents recruited from high schools at eight European sites in England, Ireland, France and Germany, followed up at ages 16, 19 and 22 with behavioural, neuropsychological, MRI and genome-wide data, to study the genetic and neurobiological basis of impulsivity, reinforcer sensitivity and emotional reactivity and their value in predicting psychiatric disorders.

label: Munich Antidepressant Response Signature
